title: Nipro SURDIAL X Hemodialysis (HD) Machine - Arterial or Venous Pressure Reading Is Incorrect
description: Use this guide for inaccurate, unstable, or implausible arterial or venous pressure readings related to tubing, transducers, connections, or setup.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient
steps.instructions: Do not rely on questionable arterial or venous pressure monitoring during dialysis. If the readings are unreliable during treatment, follow clinical procedures to maintain patient safety and transfer to another verified machine when necessary. Expected outcome: The patient is not dependent on unreliable extracorporeal pressure monitoring.

steps.title: 2. Confirm Which Pressure Reading Is Affected
steps.instructions: Determine whether the problem affects: Arterial pressure Venous pressure Both A fixed value A fluctuating value An implausible value before connection A reading that changes when tubing is moved Record any associated alarm. Expected outcome: The affected pressure channel and failure pattern are identified.

steps.title: 3. Inspect Pressure Lines and External Connections
steps.instructions: Check the associated pressure-monitoring tubing and external connections for: Kinks Occlusion Loose fittings Disconnection Cracked tubing Moisture where it should not be present Incorrect routing Do not allow fluid into areas intended to remain dry. Expected outcome: The pressure line is intact, correctly routed, and securely connected.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the Transducer Protector or Equivalent Disposable Interface
steps.instructions: Verify the disposable pressure interface is correctly installed and not wet, blocked, damaged, or contaminated. If contamination or fluid intrusion is suspected at the machine-side connection, remove the device from clinical use until evaluated according to approved procedures. Expected outcome: The disposable pressure interface is dry, unobstructed, and properly installed.

steps.title: 5. Verify Extracorporeal Circuit Setup
steps.instructions: Have qualified dialysis staff verify the blood tubing set is correctly loaded and that clamps, chambers, and access connections are positioned as intended. A circuit restriction or setup problem may produce a real abnormal pressure rather than an inaccurate measurement. Expected outcome: The circuit contains no obvious external restriction or setup error explaining the pressure reading.

steps.title: 6. Compare With a Known-Good Disposable Setup
steps.instructions: When appropriate, replace the suspect disposable pressure component or circuit with an approved known-good set during nonpatient testing. Do not reuse a questionable disposable solely for troubleshooting convenience. Expected outcome: Pressure behavior returns to normal if the disposable was the cause. If so, complete verification and stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 7. Check Baseline Behavior Without Patient Connection
steps.instructions: Using the approved preparation or test condition, observe whether arterial and venous pressure readings behave plausibly before patient use. Do not perform unauthorized calibration adjustments. Expected outcome: Pressure channels demonstrate stable and appropriate baseline behavior.

steps.title: 8. Verify With Approved Test Equipment
steps.instructions: If required, test pressure measurement performance using manufacturer-approved procedures and calibrated test equipment. Differentiate between a true circuit pressure problem and a machine measurement problem. Expected outcome: Pressure measurement performance passes the approved verification. Troubleshooting can stop.

CCR.Complaint: Dialysis staff reported the SURDIAL X venous pressure reading was unstable during setup.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the disposable venous pressure line kinked near its connection.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering corrected the tubing routing, repeated the approved setup and pressure checks, verified stable readings, and returned the machine to service.

helpfulDetails: Arterial, venous, or both channels affected
Whether fluid entered the monitoring connection

title: Nipro SURDIAL X Hemodialysis (HD) Machine - Blood Leak or Air Detector Alarm Repeats
description: Use this guide for repeated blood-leak or air-detection alarms caused by disposables, fluid conditions, positioning, contamination, or detector-related faults.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient Immediately
steps.instructions: Repeated blood-leak or air-detection alarms involve critical dialysis safety systems. Do not bypass, silence without correction, or defeat these protections. If a patient is connected, follow clinical procedures to maintain patient safety and treatment continuity. Use another verified machine if the cause cannot be safely corrected through normal clinical workflow. Expected outcome: The patient is protected and no critical detector is being bypassed.

steps.title: 2. Identify Which Alarm Is Occurring
steps.instructions: Determine whether the machine is reporting: Blood leak Air detection Both at different times An intermittent detector warning A persistent alarm immediately after setup Record the exact message and when it occurs. Expected outcome: The specific detector path and operating condition associated with the alarm are known.

steps.title: 3. Inspect the Extracorporeal Circuit for Air
steps.instructions: For air-related alarms, have qualified clinical staff inspect the blood tubing and chamber arrangement according to facility procedure. Check externally for: Visible air Incorrect chamber fill level Loose bloodline connection Cracked or damaged tubing Tubing improperly positioned in the detector Improperly seated disposable components Do not bypass the detector to continue therapy. Expected outcome: The blood circuit is correctly assembled, properly filled, and positioned without visible air or damaged tubing.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the Blood Leak Detection Area
steps.instructions: For blood-leak alarms, check the accessible detector area and dialysate path for visible contamination, moisture, residue, or improperly seated external components. A detector area contaminated during prior handling or disinfection may create false indications. Clean only using approved procedures and materials. Expected outcome: The detector area is clean, dry, and unobstructed.

steps.title: 5. Verify the Disposable Set and Placement
steps.instructions: Confirm that the approved disposable set is appropriate for the machine and has been installed according to normal clinical setup. Inspect for: Twisted tubing Flattened tubing Misrouting Poor detector alignment Damaged segments Incorrectly installed chambers or holders If appropriate and permitted, use a new approved disposable set to rule out a defective disposable. Expected outcome: The disposable circuit is compatible, undamaged, and correctly positioned. If the alarm disappears with a known-good disposable, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 6. Check for Fluid or Optical Interference
steps.instructions: Inspect accessible sensor windows and surrounding surfaces for residue, condensation, fingerprints, fluid splash, or other material that could interfere with detection. Do not insert tools into sensor assemblies or alter detector alignment. Expected outcome: Accessible sensing surfaces are clean and free of external interference.

steps.title: 7. Reproduce the Alarm Without a Patient
steps.instructions: After correcting obvious external conditions, perform the approved setup and machine checks without a patient attached. Observe whether the alarm returns under controlled conditions. Expected outcome: The detector passes normal startup or preparation checks without repeated false alarms.

steps.title: 8. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Before clinical use, confirm that: Required detector checks pass No repeated false alarm occurs Disposable positioning remains correct Relevant alarms remain functional Applicable pre-treatment tests complete successfully Never return the machine to service based solely on temporarily clearing the alarm. Expected outcome: Detection systems operate normally and required checks pass. Troubleshooting can stop.

CCR.Complaint: Dialysis staff reported repeated air detector alarms during SURDIAL X setup.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the bloodline tubing was not fully seated in the detector channel.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering corrected tubing placement, repeated the approved setup checks, verified normal detector operation with no repeated alarm, and returned the unit to service.

helpfulDetails: Disposable lot or type if relevant

title: Nipro SURDIAL X Hemodialysis (HD) Machine - Blood Pump Will Not Run or Speed Is Unstable
description: Use this guide when the blood pump will not start, stops unexpectedly, or runs inconsistently because of setup, tubing, controls, or external conditions.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot an unreliable blood pump while a patient depends on it. If the pump stops or becomes unstable during treatment, follow the facility's dialysis procedures for maintaining extracorporeal circuit and patient safety and move to another verified machine when necessary. Expected outcome: The patient is protected before technical troubleshooting begins.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Pump Symptom
steps.instructions: Determine whether the blood pump: Does not start Starts and immediately stops Runs intermittently Appears mechanically irregular Shows an unstable displayed speed Stops only when another alarm occurs Record the exact associated alarm or message. Expected outcome: The failure pattern and whether the pump is the primary problem are established.

steps.title: 3. Check for Active Alarms or Safety Interlocks
steps.instructions: Review the machine for other active conditions that may intentionally inhibit blood-pump operation. Examples include improperly loaded tubing, open doors or covers, detector alarms, pressure alarms, or other setup conditions. Do not bypass interlocks to test the pump. Expected outcome: No unresolved safety condition is intentionally preventing pump operation.

steps.title: 4. Inspect Blood Tubing Installation
steps.instructions: Inspect the pump tubing segment and verify that it is: The approved type Correctly routed Fully seated Not twisted Not flattened Not stretched improperly Free of visible damage Have clinical personnel correct the disposable setup when required. Expected outcome: The pump segment is correctly loaded and mechanically suitable for operation.

steps.title: 5. Inspect the Pump Area
steps.instructions: With the unit stopped and safe, visually inspect accessible pump components for: Foreign material Fluid contamination Obstruction Damaged accessible surfaces Improperly closed pump cover or mechanism Do not remove guards or disassemble the drive system. Expected outcome: No external obstruction or contamination prevents normal pump movement.

steps.title: 6. Verify Programmed Pump Operation
steps.instructions: Confirm the requested pump operation and speed were entered correctly for the intended setup. Do not change a clinical prescription merely to compensate for unstable machine behavior. Expected outcome: Pump settings are appropriate and the problem is not caused by an incorrect control setting.

steps.title: 7. Test With an Approved Known-Good Disposable Setup
steps.instructions: During nonpatient testing, substitute an approved known-good blood tubing set if the installed tubing is questionable. Observe whether pump operation becomes stable. Expected outcome: The pump operates normally with a known-good disposable if the original tubing caused the problem. If so, complete final verification and stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 8. Observe Pump Operation Without a Patient
steps.instructions: Run the appropriate approved setup or test process and observe the blood pump through its normal operating range required for verification. Look for repeated stopping, unusual noise, visible irregular motion, or discrepancy between commanded and observed operation. Expected outcome: Pump operation is smooth and stable without unexplained stopping.

steps.title: 9. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Complete manufacturer-approved blood-pump and alarm checks as applicable. Confirm: Stable operation Proper response to controls No recurring alarm No abnormal sound Required protective functions remain active Expected outcome: Blood-pump operation passes required verification. Troubleshooting can stop and the machine may be returned to service.

CCR.Complaint: Dialysis staff reported the SURDIAL X blood pump would start but stop intermittently during setup.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the pump tubing segment twisted and not fully seated in the pump track.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering installed the tubing correctly, repeated the approved setup checks, verified stable pump operation, and returned the machine to service.

helpfulDetails: Pump would not start or was unstable

title: Nipro SURDIAL X Hemodialysis (HD) Machine - Concentrate, Solution, or Disposable Is Not Detected
description: Use this guide when an approved concentrate, solution, or disposable is not recognized because of selection, connection, compatibility, positioning, or detection issues.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient
steps.instructions: Do not begin or continue dialysis if the required concentrate, solution, or disposable cannot be reliably recognized. Use another verified machine or correct the setup before treatment proceeds. Expected outcome: Patient treatment does not proceed with an unverified fluid or disposable configuration.

steps.title: 2. Confirm What Is Not Being Detected
steps.instructions: Identify the specific item involved and determine whether: It is never recognized Recognition is intermittent Recognition is lost when moved The issue occurs with one item only Multiple approved items fail The machine displays a specific message Record the exact message. Expected outcome: The affected item and pattern of failure are clearly identified.

steps.title: 3. Verify the Correct Approved Item
steps.instructions: Confirm that the concentrate, solution, or disposable is appropriate for the intended SURDIAL X setup and treatment. Check labeling and packaging for: Correct product Correct intended use Obvious damage Contamination Improper storage evidence Expired or otherwise unsuitable product according to facility policy Do not substitute unapproved products. Expected outcome: The correct approved item is being used.

steps.title: 4. Inspect Physical Installation and Connections
steps.instructions: Verify that the item is fully installed in its normal operating position. Check for: Loose or incomplete connection Incorrect orientation Twisted or kinked tubing Misaligned disposable component Connector damage Fluid or residue on accessible sensing surfaces Expected outcome: The item is correctly seated and connected without visible damage.

steps.title: 5. Inspect Accessible Detection Areas
steps.instructions: Examine accessible sensor, holder, connector, or detection surfaces for contamination, moisture, residue, or obstruction. Clean only according to approved procedures. Do not modify sensors, magnets, tags, switches, or interlocks to force recognition. Expected outcome: The detection area is clean, dry, and unobstructed.

steps.title: 6. Test a Known-Good Approved Item
steps.instructions: When clinically and technically appropriate, substitute another known-good approved concentrate container, solution source, or disposable of the correct type. Observe whether recognition is restored. Expected outcome: If the replacement is recognized normally, the original item is isolated as the cause and troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 7. Check Configuration and Selection
steps.instructions: Verify that machine setup selections match the installed item and intended therapy. Do not enter unauthorized configuration menus or alter service-level settings. If a prescription-related selection is involved, have qualified clinical staff verify it. Expected outcome: The selected machine configuration matches the installed approved product.

steps.title: 8. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Repeat the normal preparation sequence and confirm: The item remains recognized Required fluid preparation proceeds normally No related alarm recurs Applicable pre-treatment tests pass Expected outcome: Recognition is stable through preparation and verification. Troubleshooting can stop.

CCR.Complaint: Dialysis staff reported the SURDIAL X would not recognize the connected concentrate during setup.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the concentrate connector was not fully engaged at the machine connection.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering reseated the connection, repeated preparation, verified stable concentrate recognition and required checks, and returned the machine to service.

title: Nipro SURDIAL X Hemodialysis (HD) Machine - Conductivity Will Not Stabilize or Is Out of Range
description: Use this guide for unstable or abnormal conductivity associated with concentrate supply, water, connections, configuration, or another externally verifiable condition.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Stop Use of Unreliable Dialysate
steps.instructions: Do not continue patient treatment when dialysate conductivity is unstable, outside the machine's acceptable condition, or cannot be independently verified as appropriate. Move the patient to another verified machine or follow the facility's dialysis contingency process. Expected outcome: No patient is dependent on a machine with questionable dialysate composition.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Reported Condition
steps.instructions: Determine when the conductivity issue occurs: During preparation After concentrate connection During treatment setup Intermittently during operation Only with one concentrate source After a room, water, or supply change Record any machine message exactly. Expected outcome: The timing and repeatability of the conductivity problem are established.

steps.title: 3. Verify the Water Supply Condition
steps.instructions: Confirm that the machine has its normal approved water supply and that facility water-treatment systems are operating normally. Check for: Interrupted water flow Kinked or restricted external water connection Recent water-system maintenance Multiple dialysis machines showing similar symptoms Do not adjust facility water-treatment settings unless authorized. Expected outcome: The dialysis machine is receiving its expected external water supply. A facility-wide problem is identified and escalated if multiple machines are affected.

steps.title: 4. Inspect Concentrate Containers and Connections
steps.instructions: Verify the correct concentrate products intended for the prescribed treatment are present and connected to the correct external connection points. Inspect for: Empty or nearly empty containers Loose connections Kinked tubing Cracked tubing or fittings Incorrect concentrate selection Obvious contamination Improperly seated pickup connections Do not substitute unapproved fluids. Expected outcome: Correct concentrate sources are available and securely connected without visible restriction or leakage.

steps.title: 5. Check for Concentrate Supply or Batch Isolation
steps.instructions: If permitted by facility procedure, compare the issue using another approved container or source of the same required concentrate. If multiple machines show the same conductivity problem from a common supply or batch, stop using that source and escalate appropriately. Expected outcome: The concentrate source is either ruled out or identified as the external cause. If conductivity stabilizes with an approved known-good source, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 6. Verify Treatment Configuration
steps.instructions: Confirm the treatment setup and concentrate selection match the intended prescription and facility workflow. Do not alter clinical prescription values merely to force conductivity into an acceptable state. If a configuration appears incorrect, have qualified clinical personnel verify the prescription and setup before continuing. Expected outcome: The machine configuration corresponds to the intended treatment and no incorrect selection is producing the conductivity issue.

steps.title: 7. Inspect Accessible External Fluid Connections
steps.instructions: Inspect accessible dialysate-related connections for leakage, incomplete seating, crossed connections, or restriction. Do not disconnect or manipulate internal fluid-path components beyond approved external service actions. Expected outcome: External fluid connections are secure, correctly routed, and free of visible leakage or obstruction.

steps.title: 8. Reprepare and Observe Conductivity
steps.instructions: After correcting any external supply or connection problem, perform the approved preparation sequence and allow the system to reach its normal ready condition. Observe whether conductivity becomes stable without repeated alarms or abnormal fluctuation. Expected outcome: Conductivity stabilizes during preparation and remains acceptable to the machine's normal monitoring system. If successful, proceed to final verification.

steps.title: 9. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Before return to service, complete applicable manufacturer-approved checks. Where facility procedure requires independent dialysate verification, use approved calibrated test equipment. Do not return the machine to service simply because an alarm cleared temporarily. Expected outcome: Conductivity remains stable and required dialysate verification passes. Troubleshooting can stop.

CCR.Complaint: Dialysis staff reported the SURDIAL X would not achieve stable conductivity during treatment preparation.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the concentrate connection was not fully seated and was intermittently drawing air.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering reseated the approved concentrate connection, repeated preparation, verified stable conductivity and required checks, and returned the machine to service.

helpfulDetails: Whether a known-good concentrate source was tested

title: Nipro SURDIAL X Hemodialysis (HD) Machine - Dialysate Temperature Is High, Low, or Unstable
description: Use this guide when dialysate temperature is abnormal or unstable due to supply, environment, setup, sensing, heating, or flow-related conditions.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient
steps.instructions: Do not continue treatment using a machine that cannot maintain appropriate dialysate temperature. Transfer the patient to another verified dialysis machine or follow the facility's clinical contingency procedure before troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The patient is no longer dependent on equipment with questionable dialysate temperature control.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Temperature Problem
steps.instructions: Determine whether the reported condition is: Temperature too high Temperature too low Slow warm-up Repeated fluctuation A displayed temperature that disagrees with an independent measurement A temperature-related alarm during preparation or treatment Record the exact displayed information. Expected outcome: The actual symptom and point of occurrence are clearly identified.

steps.title: 3. Verify Water Supply and Environmental Conditions
steps.instructions: Confirm normal facility water supply and check for environmental conditions that could affect machine operation. Look for: Unusually hot or cold incoming water Interrupted or restricted water supply Recent water-system maintenance Extreme room temperature Blocked ventilation around the machine Compare with nearby dialysis machines when appropriate. Expected outcome: The machine has a normal external water source and suitable environment.

steps.title: 4. Inspect External Fluid Connections
steps.instructions: Check accessible water and fluid connections for kinks, restrictions, leaks, or incomplete seating. Restricted fluid flow can affect temperature regulation and should be corrected before suspecting internal heating components. Expected outcome: External fluid supply and drainage connections are unobstructed and properly connected.

steps.title: 5. Verify Treatment Temperature Configuration
steps.instructions: Confirm the configured dialysate temperature corresponds to the intended treatment prescription. Do not change a prescribed treatment setting simply to compensate for a suspected machine fault. Have clinical staff verify the prescription if there is any uncertainty. Expected outcome: The programmed treatment setting is correct and not the source of the reported condition.

steps.title: 6. Allow Normal Preparation to Complete
steps.instructions: After external conditions are verified, run the machine through the approved preparation process and allow sufficient time for normal stabilization. Observe whether the temperature reaches and maintains the configured condition without repeated alarms. Expected outcome: Temperature reaches a stable ready condition. If it remains stable, continue to final verification.

steps.title: 7. Compare With Approved Independent Test Equipment
steps.instructions: When required by facility or manufacturer procedure, verify dialysate temperature using approved calibrated test equipment. Use the comparison to determine whether the problem is true dialysate temperature instability or an apparent measurement discrepancy. Expected outcome: Independent verification agrees with acceptable machine performance. If so, troubleshooting can stop after completion of all required checks.

steps.title: 8. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Confirm: Temperature remains stable No related alarms recur Conductivity and other required dialysate checks are satisfactory Fluid flow and preparation remain normal Applicable return-to-service testing passes Expected outcome: The machine maintains appropriate dialysate conditions through the verification period and may be returned to service.

CCR.Complaint: Dialysis staff reported the SURDIAL X dialysate temperature remained low and would not stabilize during preparation.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the external water inlet hose partially kinked behind the machine.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering corrected the hose routing, repeated preparation, verified stable dialysate temperature and required checks, and returned the unit to service.

title: Nipro SURDIAL X Hemodialysis (HD) Machine - Disinfection, Rinse, or Drain Cycle Will Not Complete
description: Use this guide when a disinfection, rinse, or drain cycle stops, repeats, or cannot finish because of external fluid, drainage, setup, or service conditions.

steps.title: 1. Keep the Machine Out of Patient Service
steps.instructions: Do not use a dialysis machine clinically if a required disinfection, rinse, or drain process has not completed successfully. Clearly identify the unit as unavailable until the cycle issue is resolved and required post-process verification is complete. Expected outcome: No patient is placed on a machine with an incomplete cleaning or fluid-preparation process.

steps.title: 2. Confirm Which Cycle Fails
steps.instructions: Determine whether the failure occurs during: Disinfection Rinse Drain Initial fill Transition between cycle stages Final completion Record the exact message and the point at which the cycle stops. Expected outcome: The failed cycle stage is identified and reproducible.

steps.title: 3. Verify Water Supply
steps.instructions: Confirm the machine has normal approved water supply. Inspect accessible supply connections for: Closed or interrupted source Kinked hose Loose connection Leakage Facility water-system issue Check whether other dialysis machines are experiencing similar problems. Expected outcome: Adequate external water supply is available.

steps.title: 4. Verify Drainage
steps.instructions: Inspect the external drain path for: Kinks Pinching Obstruction Incorrect placement Backflow Loose or leaking connection A restricted drain can prevent multiple cleaning cycles from completing. Expected outcome: The drain path is open and properly routed.

steps.title: 5. Verify Required Solution and Connections
steps.instructions: For cycles requiring an approved chemical or solution, verify the correct product and normal connection are present. Inspect the external pickup connection and tubing for: Empty source Loose connection Kink Cracking Improper placement Do not substitute unapproved chemicals or concentrations. Expected outcome: Required external solution is available and correctly connected.

steps.title: 6. Check Machine Setup and Cycle Selection
steps.instructions: Confirm the intended cycle was selected and that any normal prerequisites required by the machine's standard workflow have been satisfied. Do not alter service-level cleaning parameters or bypass cycle stages. Expected outcome: The cycle has been initiated under the correct normal operating conditions.

steps.title: 7. Inspect for Visible Fluid Leakage
steps.instructions: Check the floor, rear connections, accessible hose connections, and exterior of the machine for leakage. If unexplained fluid is originating from inside the unit, stop troubleshooting and remove it from service. Expected outcome: No uncorrected leak is present.

steps.title: 8. Restart the Cycle After Correcting External Causes
steps.instructions: If no hazard exists, restart the approved cycle after correcting water, drain, solution, or setup issues. Do not repeatedly restart a cycle that stops at the same point without identifying a cause. Expected outcome: The selected disinfection, rinse, or drain cycle completes normally.

steps.title: 9. Perform Required Post-Cycle Verification
steps.instructions: Before return to patient service, complete all applicable manufacturer and facility verification associated with the completed process. Ensure the machine is in the proper ready condition and that no residual cycle-related alarm remains. Expected outcome: The cycle is complete, required verification passes, and the machine is suitable for return to service. Troubleshooting can stop.

CCR.Complaint: Dialysis staff reported the SURDIAL X rinse cycle repeatedly stopped before completion.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the external drain hose kinked behind the machine and restricting flow.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering corrected the drain hose routing, repeated the rinse cycle, verified successful completion and required post-cycle checks, and returned the machine to service.

title: Nipro SURDIAL X Hemodialysis (HD) Machine - Network, Treatment Record, or Data Export Fails
description: Use this guide when network communication, treatment-record transfer, or data export fails because of connections, infrastructure, configuration, or external systems.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Preserve Treatment Continuity
steps.instructions: Determine whether the communication failure affects dialysis therapy itself or only documentation and data transfer. Do not interrupt safe treatment solely to troubleshoot a nonessential network problem unless required by clinical policy. If communication is required for safe care, provide an approved alternate documentation or workflow method. Expected outcome: Patient care continues safely while the communication problem is evaluated.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Communication Failure
steps.instructions: Determine whether the issue involves: No network connection Missing treatment record Failed data export Intermittent transfer Incorrect patient association Failure to communicate with an external system Failure affecting one machine or multiple machines Record any displayed network or export message exactly. Expected outcome: The affected communication path and scope are identified.

steps.title: 3. Verify the Physical Network Connection
steps.instructions: Inspect accessible network cabling and connectors for: Loose connection Damaged latch Bent or damaged connector Crushed cable Disconnected wall jack Cable routed under equipment or furniture If permitted, reseat the connection. Expected outcome: The physical communication connection is secure and visibly intact.

steps.title: 4. Check Link or Connection Status
steps.instructions: Observe available normal network or communication indicators without entering unauthorized service menus. Compare the affected machine with another working SURDIAL X or nearby supported device when practical. Expected outcome: A physical network connection is present, or the absence of one identifies the next troubleshooting direction.

steps.title: 5. Test the External Network Path
steps.instructions: Use an approved known-good network cable or known-good active connection point when facility policy allows. Coordinate with IT before moving the device to a different network segment or making infrastructure changes. Expected outcome: A failed external cable or port is either isolated or ruled out.

steps.title: 6. Determine Whether the Problem Is Device-Specific
steps.instructions: Check whether: Other dialysis machines can communicate The receiving application is operational The issue is limited to one room or switch Multiple devices lost connectivity simultaneously Recent network maintenance occurred Do not change network settings simply because the device is offline. Expected outcome: The problem is classified as device-specific, infrastructure-related, or receiving-system related.

steps.title: 7. Verify Approved Network Configuration
steps.instructions: Compare the affected machine's approved network configuration with documented facility records or a known-good equivalent device. Check items such as assigned network identity and communication settings only within authorized access levels. Do not alter addresses, interface parameters, or application settings without coordination with the responsible IT or integration team. Expected outcome: The machine's approved configuration is confirmed or an authorized configuration discrepancy is identified.

steps.title: 8. Verify the Treatment Record or Export Destination
steps.instructions: Confirm the intended external destination is available and that the correct workflow is being used. Determine whether the issue is: Record not created Record created but not transmitted Record transmitted but not received Export destination unavailable Patient association mismatch Preserve existing treatment information and avoid unnecessary deletion or recreation of records. Expected outcome: The failure point between the machine and receiving system is narrowed down.

steps.title: 9. Perform an Approved Communication Test
steps.instructions: After correcting any cable, port, or authorized configuration issue, perform a controlled test transaction or data export according to facility procedure. Verify receipt at the intended destination rather than relying only on a local "sent" indication. Expected outcome: Data passes through the complete communication path and is confirmed at the receiving system. Troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 10. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Confirm: Network connection remains stable A test record or approved data transfer succeeds The receiving system receives the information correctly No unintended patient association or duplicate record was created Dialysis functions remain unaffected Expected outcome: The complete network and data-transfer path is verified and the machine may be returned to normal clinical workflow.

CCR.Complaint: Dialysis staff reported treatment records from one SURDIAL X were no longer reaching the receiving system.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the network cable at the machine had a damaged retaining tab and was intermittently disconnecting.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering replaced the damaged cable, verified stable network connectivity and successful end-to-end treatment-record transfer, and returned the machine to service.

helpfulDetails: Whether one or multiple machines were affected

title: Nipro SURDIAL X Hemodialysis (HD) Machine - System Will Not Power On or Complete Startup
description: Use this guide when the SURDIAL X has no power, stops during startup, or does not reach a ready condition after basic external checks.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Maintain Continuity of Care
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot a dialysis machine while a patient depends on it if power or startup is unreliable. If treatment is underway, follow the facility's clinical procedure for safely transferring or discontinuing therapy and provide another verified dialysis machine. Check for smoke, unusual odor, liquid intrusion, overheating, damaged power components, or other obvious hazards. Remove the machine from service immediately if any are present. Expected outcome: The patient is protected, treatment continuity is addressed, and the machine is safe for controlled troubleshooting.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Startup Failure
steps.instructions: Determine whether the machine: Has no display or indicators Powers briefly and shuts down Stops at a startup screen Reboots repeatedly Displays an alarm or message Starts but never reaches the normal ready state Record any displayed message exactly rather than interpreting it. Expected outcome: The exact failure point is identified and can be reproduced without a patient connected.

steps.title: 3. Verify the AC Power Source
steps.instructions: Confirm the power cord is fully seated and visually inspect the cord, plug, strain relief, and accessible inlet for damage. Test the wall receptacle using approved test equipment or another known-good method permitted by facility policy. Avoid relying only on the fact that another nearby outlet appears to work. If the unit is connected through an approved branch-power arrangement, verify that arrangement has not been switched off or interrupted. Expected outcome: A verified AC source is available and the external power path is intact. If normal startup now completes, troubleshooting can stop after final verification.

steps.title: 4. Check External Power Controls and Connections
steps.instructions: Verify the machine's normal operator-accessible power switch or controls are correctly positioned. Inspect accessible external connectors that are required for normal startup. Look for partially seated plugs, bent connector shells, contamination, fluid exposure, or cables being pulled tight. Do not open covers or bypass protective interlocks. Expected outcome: Required external connections are secure and no visible external defect is interfering with startup.

steps.title: 5. Remove Nonessential External Accessories
steps.instructions: With the machine safely shut down, disconnect nonessential external peripherals or communication accessories that can be removed without changing the dialysis fluid path or bypassing required safety systems. Restart the machine using the normal startup procedure. Expected outcome: The machine completes startup with only required components connected. If an external accessory was preventing startup, isolate that accessory from use and document the finding.

steps.title: 6. Evaluate the Environment
steps.instructions: Confirm the machine is not exposed to: Obstructed ventilation Excessive heat or cold Standing water or recent fluid spill Condensation Damaged power infrastructure Recent electrical outage or power-quality event Allow environmental conditions to return to an acceptable operating state before retesting when appropriate. Expected outcome: No external environmental condition is preventing reliable startup.

steps.title: 7. Perform a Controlled Restart
steps.instructions: If no hazard is present, shut the machine down normally, allow it to fully power off, and restart it once. Do not repeatedly cycle power in an attempt to force the machine past a persistent startup fault. Observe whether the same failure occurs at the same point. Expected outcome: The SURDIAL X reaches its normal ready state without unexpected shutdown, restart, or persistent startup fault. If successful, continue to final verification.

steps.title: 8. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Before returning the machine to service, confirm: Normal startup completes Displays and controls respond Expected self-checks complete Required alarms and indicators are available No abnormal sound, odor, heat, or message remains Applicable pre-treatment machine checks can be completed Use approved manufacturer documentation and test equipment for any required return-to-service testing. Expected outcome: The machine starts reliably and completes required verification. Troubleshooting can stop and the unit may be returned to service according to facility policy.

CCR.Complaint: Dialysis staff reported the Nipro SURDIAL X would power on but would not complete startup.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the machine was connected to a receptacle that did not provide reliable AC power.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering verified a functional receptacle, restarted the machine, confirmed normal startup and pre-treatment checks, and returned the unit to service.

title: Nipro SURDIAL X Hemodialysis (HD) Machine - Ultrafiltration or Fluid-Balance Test Fails
description: Use this guide when ultrafiltration or fluid-balance verification fails because of fluid supply, connections, setup, leaks, drainage, or service-level faults.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient
steps.instructions: Do not use the machine for patient treatment when ultrafiltration or fluid-balance performance cannot be verified. Use another tested dialysis machine until the affected unit passes all required checks. Expected outcome: No treatment begins on a machine with unverified fluid-removal accuracy.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Failed Test
steps.instructions: Determine whether the issue involves: A startup fluid-balance check An ultrafiltration verification An interrupted test A repeated alarm A result that is inconsistent between attempts A failure following maintenance or disinfection Record the exact message and test conditions. Expected outcome: The specific test and repeatable failure condition are identified.

steps.title: 3. Check Water Supply and Drainage
steps.instructions: Verify that external water supply and drainage are available and unobstructed. Inspect accessible hoses for: Kinks Pinching Leakage Loose connections Improper drain placement Backflow or drainage restriction indications Expected outcome: The machine has stable water supply and free drainage.

steps.title: 4. Inspect Concentrate and Fluid Connections
steps.instructions: Verify required concentrate and external fluid connections are properly seated and free of leaks or restrictions. An incomplete fluid path can prevent accurate preparation or balance testing. Expected outcome: External fluid connections are complete, secure, and leak-free.

steps.title: 5. Check for Visible Leakage
steps.instructions: Inspect around the machine and accessible fluid connections for moisture, dripping, pooled fluid, or evidence of recent leakage. Do not continue operating a machine with unexplained internal or external fluid leakage. Expected outcome: No visible leak is present. If leakage is found and cannot be corrected at an approved external connection, remove the machine from service.

steps.title: 6. Verify Disposable and Treatment Setup
steps.instructions: Confirm any required disposable components or external treatment connections used during the test are correctly installed. Check for incorrect routing, open clamps, loose fittings, or components that are not fully seated. Expected outcome: External setup is correct and is not causing the balance failure.

steps.title: 7. Repeat the Approved Test Once
steps.instructions: After correcting external conditions, repeat the manufacturer-approved test under controlled nonpatient conditions. Avoid repeated cycling if the same test consistently fails. Expected outcome: The fluid-balance or ultrafiltration test completes successfully. If it passes consistently, proceed to final verification.

steps.title: 8. Verify With Approved Test Equipment When Required
steps.instructions: If the facility or manufacturer procedure calls for independent ultrafiltration or fluid-volume verification, use calibrated approved test equipment and the authorized procedure. Do not adjust internal calibration merely to make the result pass. Expected outcome: Fluid-removal or balance performance meets the approved verification criteria. Troubleshooting can stop.

CCR.Complaint: Dialysis staff reported the SURDIAL X repeatedly failed its fluid-balance check during preparation.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the external drain hose partially compressed behind the machine, restricting drainage.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering corrected the drain hose routing, repeated the approved test, verified successful fluid-balance checks, and returned the machine to service.

helpfulDetails: Whether failure followed service or disinfection
